6. Ad space. You guys seem to have a total disregard for revenue, let alone actual profit. This image by contrast is not a joke. That's from this page when Reddit started deciding to go down the path of advertising.

A company is naturally dependent upon their revenue source. It's how they get by. A company that sells gizmos only does well when their customers are happy and purchasing lots of gizmos from them. The problem with advertising is that you begin to differentiate between the users of a site and the revenue of a site. As companies become dependent on advertising, pleasing users is no longer what matters - pleasing advertisers is. Big spend advertisers end up becoming effective owners of a site. As the site becomes dependent upon their revenue, they can destroy the site by simply threatening to pull funding, and advertisers are not shy about using this power once they get their claws into a site.

A famous example in the video game industry is Jeff Gerstmann. Gerstmann was the editorial director of GameSpot, a popular gaming review site, until he decided to publish a couple of review scores that were 'too low' in the view of the advertisers funding GameSpot. These scores included a 7.5/10. Advertisers took their complaints to the executives at the company and in a situation where it was either Gerstmann leaves, or they do - the result is predictable: Gerstmann was fired. Since then games with big advertising spend on that GameSpot seem to always be great! Well... at least that's what the reviews are telling gamers in the pauses between all the articles insulting them (that have shown a great ability to produce those revenue generating clicks.)

By allowing ads on sites you support, you are encouraging and enabling these sites to become dependent upon advertising. If you truly support a site help encourage them to find a revenue source where the interest of the site is based around their consumers and not outside advertisers. By allowing ads you are not helping the companies you support, you are encouraging them to become dependent upon the very people that have a tendency of destroying many things they touch. Block those ads.
